info.title: Pod PDF Accessibility Evaluation and Remediation API
info.description:
Common web-service interface shared by Team 1 and Team 3 for cross-team testing.
Each team implements this contract independently. Tests target a team by its base URL.

Project API (pod-defined): GET /health, GET /checks, POST /process.
Course test endpoints (required on every system): POST /test/setup, GET /test/report.

State: PDFs are never stored; every /process request is independent and no reset
is needed between tests. The only state a system keeps is its list of test
sessions and the code coverage measured for each one (see /test/setup).
Sessions are kept in memory until the service restarts. No authentication is required.
Limits: maximum file size 20 MB (20,971,520 bytes); no maximum page count.
Encrypted or password-protected PDFs are not supported.
Scanned PDFs without a text layer are not supported: OCR is out of scope, so a
PDF must contain extractable text (see NO_TEXT_LAYER under POST /process).

Changes in 0.3.0: POST /evaluations renamed to POST /process; optional session_id
form field added to /process; /test/setup and /test/report added; x-pod-testing
notes added (components, acceptance criteria, sessions, timing).

Changes in 0.4.0 (Phase 4, detection): Finding.status adds "detected" for an
auto_fixable finding that was found but not repaired (repair arrives in Phase 5).
Location.description says where the issue is; fix_description says what is wrong
and how it can be fixed. POST /process takes an optional form field output:
"json" (default, unchanged) or "zip", which returns one zip file with the
uploaded PDF, the output PDF, the report PDF and result.json. Error code
INVALID_REQUEST added (400, for an output value other than json or zip).
Location.bbox added (optional, nullable): [x0, y0, x1, y1] of the finding on its
page, so a viewer can highlight it.

Changes in 0.5.0 (Phase 5: repair, scope limits, LLM suggestions):
  - Scanned PDFs: a PDF in which no page has a text layer (a scanned or
    image-only PDF) is rejected with 422 and the new error code NO_TEXT_LAYER. A
    PDF in which only some pages are scanned is still processed; those pages are
    named in limitations and no text-based findings are reported for them.
    Definitions are under POST /process ("Scanned pages").
  - LLM-assisted suggestions: a system may use a large language model for
    CHK-NONTEXT, CHK-LINK, CHK-COLOR, CHK-SENSORY and CHK-TITLE only. The other
    checks use rule-based suggestions. Rules are under POST /process
    ("Suggestions and LLM use"). All new fields are optional, so a system that
    uses no LLM still conforms.
  - Finding adds suggested_text and suggestion_source (both optional, nullable).
  - Repair adds method ("rule" or "llm", optional, default "rule") and
    applied_text (optional, nullable).

servers.description: Base URL supplied by the team under test (never hard-coded)

x-pod-testing.description: Pod rules for the course's cross-team testing interface. Each team's tester calls a target system's /test/setup, then the project API below, then the target's /test/report, and returns one suite report.
x-pod-testing.setup_data: Testers send {"session_id": "<uuid>", "setup": {}}. No starting data is needed.
x-pod-testing.session_identification: Testers send the session ID as the optional session_id form field on every POST /process request, so the system can attribute code coverage to that session. GET /health and GET /checks take no session ID. A /process request without a session_id, or with an unknown one, is still processed normally; it just is not counted toward any session's coverage.
x-pod-testing.resets_and_cleanup: None needed. /process keeps no data between requests, so tests may run in any order and do not interfere. Session records are kept until the service restarts.
x-pod-testing.llm_outputs: LLM text differs between runs and between systems. Tests may check that suggested_text is present, that suggestion_source and Repair.method use the allowed values, and that LLM use stays within the allowed checks, but never compare LLM-written text word for word. A test must pass when a system uses no LLM, or when its LLM was unavailable and it fell back to rule-based text.
x-pod-testing.concurrency: Multiple sessions may exist at once. A system may process session-tagged requests one at a time to measure coverage accurately.

timing.retries: Testers do not retry project calls. A call with no response within 60 seconds is recorded as outcome "error" with source "communication".

components.description: Component coverage counts how many of these components the suite exercised. A component is exercised when at least one test sends a request whose expected response depends on that component.

list.name: Automatic repair
list.exercised_by: a /process test with an auto-fixable issue that checks repairs and output_pdf

list.name: Accessibility report output
list.exercised_by: a /process test checking report_pdf and compliance_statement

system_coverage.description: System coverage counts how many of the pod's acceptance criteria (Phase 2 report, Section 4.1) the suite exercised. A criterion is exercised when at least one test performs the check that criterion describes.

get.summary: Confirm the service is reachable before a test run
get.description: Lets the cross-team test harness confirm that a team's base URL is live and which version of this spec it implements. No state change.

get.summary: List the accessibility checks this implementation performs
get.description: Returns the pod's agreed check set, each with its WCAG 2.1 success criterion, level, and classification, so both teams can confirm they evaluate the same things before results are compared. No state change.

200.description: The agreed check set implemented by this service

post.summary: Evaluate a PDF, repair safe issues, re-validate, and return results
post.description:
Runs the full pipeline on one uploaded PDF in a single request:
validate input, run all eight agreed checks, classify each issue,
repair auto-fixable issues on a copy, re-run the affected checks, and
return the output PDF, the accessibility report PDF, and structured results.

Processing stages (state changes within one request):
  1. RECEIVED     - file arrives; nothing has been evaluated yet
  2. VALIDATED    - file type, readability, encryption/password, and size checked;
                    any failure ends the request with an error response (status: error)
  3. EVALUATED    - every check listed in checks_performed has run; findings recorded
  4. CLASSIFIED   - each finding is auto_fixable or human_review, never both
  5. REPAIRED     - only CHK-TITLE and CHK-LANG findings are fixed, on a copy;
                    the uploaded file is never changed
  6. REVALIDATED  - CHK-TITLE and CHK-LANG re-run on the repaired copy
  7. REPORTED     - output PDF, report PDF, and JSON results returned (status: completed)
Nothing about the PDF is stored after the response is sent. If session_id names a
session created by /test/setup, the system also records code coverage for it.

Output format (form field output):
  - json (default): the EvaluationResult as JSON. Testers use this.
  - zip: the same result as one downloadable zip file (application/zip,
    Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<file stem>_results.zip") containing:
      original.pdf            the uploaded PDF, byte for byte
      <output_pdf.file_name>  the output (repaired) PDF
      <report_pdf.file_name>  the accessibility report PDF
      result.json             the EvaluationResult, except that output_pdf and
                              report_pdf have no content_base64 (they are the
                              files above)
    Validation errors are still returned as JSON Error responses.

Suggestions and LLM use:
  - Every finding has fix_description: what is wrong and how to fix it, in
    plain words. A system may add suggested_text: the concrete text it proposes
    (alt text, link text, a rewritten sentence, a title). suggestion_source
    says who wrote it: "rule" (fixed or template text) or "llm".
  - An LLM may be used only for these checks:
      CHK-NONTEXT  draft alt text for an image (the model sees the image)
      CHK-LINK     descriptive link text from the sentence and the link target
      CHK-COLOR    the sentence rewritten so it does not rely on color alone
      CHK-SENSORY  the sentence rewritten so it does not rely on shape,
                   position or sound
      CHK-TITLE    a title suggested from the document's content
    CHK-LANG, CHK-HEADINGS and CHK-STRUCTURE use rule-based suggestions only.
  - What may be written into output_pdf:
      CHK-TITLE (auto_fixable): the title, which may be LLM-suggested. The
        repair is recorded with method "llm" and applied_text, and the
        finding's status is fixed or repair_failed as for any repair.
      CHK-NONTEXT, CHK-LINK (human_review): LLM-drafted alt text, or a link's
        accessible label, may be written into the PDF. The visible page
        content is not changed. The repair is recorded with method "llm" and
        applied_text, but the finding is not resolved: its status stays
        needs_human_review, it stays in human_review_items, and it is not
        counted in summary.fixed_count. Its validation_result says only
        whether the text was written correctly, not whether it is accurate.
      CHK-COLOR, CHK-SENSORY: suggestions only. The system never rewrites the
        document's visible text.
  - LLM text is always marked: suggestion_source "llm" in the result, and
    labeled "AI-generated, please verify" in the report PDF.
  - If the LLM is unavailable, slow or rate-limited, the system falls back to
    rule-based suggestions (suggestion_source "rule"), still returns 200, and
    names the affected checks in limitations. An LLM failure is never
    returned as EXTERNAL_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE or PROCESSING_ERROR, and LLM
    calls count toward the 60-second project call limit.
  - When an LLM was used, limitations says that document content (text, and
    images for CHK-NONTEXT) was sent to an external model provider.

Scanned pages (OCR is out of scope):
  - A page has a text layer when text can be extracted from it: at least one
    non-whitespace character (for example PyMuPDF page.get_text()). Invisible
    OCR text counts, so a PDF that has already been through OCR is accepted.
  - A scanned page is a page with no text layer that shows at least one image.
    A blank page (no text and no image) is not a scanned page.
  - No page has a text layer (scanned, image-only or blank PDF): 422
    NO_TEXT_LAYER. This check runs after the PDF has been opened, so a
    corrupted, encrypted or password-protected file gets its own error first.
  - Some pages are scanned: the PDF is processed. limitations names every
    scanned page (for example "Pages 3 and 5 are scanned (no text layer); OCR
    is not supported, so text-based checks did not run on them"), and no
    findings from text-based checks (CHK-SENSORY, CHK-COLOR, CHK-LINK, and the
    untagged-heading part of CHK-HEADINGS) are reported for those pages. The
    other checks still run on them, for example CHK-NONTEXT for the page image.

How to interpret a 200 response:
  - outcome says whether any repairs were applied.
  - Every finding has exactly one classification and one final status.
  - repairs lists each attempted fix and whether it passed re-validation.
  - new_issues_after_repair lists problems the repairs introduced.
  - needs_human_review findings are unresolved by design, not system failures.
  - An empty array means "none found", never "not checked".
  - checks_performed lists only the checks that actually ran. Until all eight are
    implemented (Phase 4), a check missing from this list was not performed and
    must be named in limitations.
  - compliance_statement is fixed text; a 200 never means the PDF is compliant.
  - A page named in limitations as scanned was not checked for text-based
    issues; no text-based findings on it means "not checked", not "none found".
  - A repair with method "llm" on a human_review finding means AI text was
    written into the PDF for a person to verify; it does not resolve the finding.

file.description: The PDF to evaluate. Must be a readable PDF, no larger than 20,971,520 bytes, not encrypted or password-protected, and with a text layer on at least one page (scanned PDFs need OCR first).

session_id.description: Optional. Test session ID from /test/setup, so the system can attribute code coverage to that session. Missing or unknown IDs do not change the response.

output.description: Optional. "json" (default) returns the EvaluationResult as JSON. "zip" returns one zip file with original.pdf, the output PDF, the report PDF and result.json (see the description above).

200.description: Processing completed. JSON (EvaluationResult) by default; with output=zip, a zip file containing original.pdf, the output PDF, the report PDF and result.json.

location.description: Image on page 2 with alt text "image1"

findings.fix_description: Alt text "image1" is a placeholder; describe what the image shows. An AI draft was added to the output PDF; please verify it.
findings.suggested_text: Bar chart of monthly enrollment from January to June, rising from 120 to 310 students.

repairs.action: Wrote AI-drafted alt text to Figure 1
repairs.applied_text: Bar chart of monthly enrollment from January to June, rising from 120 to 310 students.

limitations: and 2.4.6 require human judgment and were not repaired
AI-generated alt text was written for Figure 1 and must be verified by a person
Document content (text and images) was sent to an external language model provider for suggestions
example.compliance_statement: This report does not certify ADA Title II or WCAG 2.1 conformance.

400.description: No file was attached (REQ-02), or output is not "json" or "zip"

value.message: Request must include a PDF in the 'file' field.

post.summary: Prepare a test session (course cross-team testing interface)
post.description: Called by a tester (or by staff) before a suite runs. Registers the supplied session ID so later /process calls tagged with it are counted toward its code coverage. No starting data is needed, so the session is ready immediately. Does not run tests. Must stay reachable at all times.

201.description: Session ready; the same ID is returned

409.description: A session with this ID already exists

500.description: Preparation failed; the tester returns this to its caller and does not run the suite

get.summary: Code coverage measured for a session (course cross-team testing interface)
get.description: Returns the code coverage measured for this session's /process requests since setup. Reading it does not change it and does not run any project operation. Setup completes synchronously, so 409 (preparation in progress) is never returned by systems that follow this spec.

200.description: Coverage measured so far for this session

code.basis: Source lines executed while handling this session's POST /process requests since setup

TestBadRequest.description: Invalid request to a course test endpoint

MissingFile.description: No file was attached to the request (REQ-02)

example.message: Request must include a PDF in the 'file' field.
File exceeds the 20 MB project limit.
Input must be a PDF file.

UnprocessablePdf.description: File is a PDF but cannot be processed because it is corrupted, unreadable, encrypted, password-protected, or has no text layer on any page (a scanned PDF; OCR is not supported) (REQ-02)

value.message: PDF is password-protected and cannot be opened.
Scanned PDFs without a text layer are not supported; run OCR first.

ProcessingError.description: Processing failed after the file was accepted. Returned as an explicit error instead of an unhandled crash (REQ-16)

example.message: Evaluation could not be completed for this file.

ExternalServiceUnavailable.description: A required external service was unavailable. Reported separately so it is not counted as a test failure of the implementation

example.message: A required external service is unavailable; retry later.

bbox.description: Optional. Where the finding is on `page`, as [x0, y0, x1, y1] in PDF user space (points, origin at the bottom left, before page rotation), so a viewer can highlight it. Null or absent when only the page (or nothing) is known.

status.description: detected: auto_fixable and found, not repaired (no repair attempted). fixed / repair_failed: a repair was attempted and re-validated. needs_human_review: human_review findings, never repaired automatically.

fix_description.description: What is wrong and how it can be fixed, in plain words.

suggested_text.description: Optional. The concrete text proposed for the fix (alt text, link text, a rewritten sentence, a title). null or absent when there is none.

suggestion_source.description: Optional. Who wrote suggested_text: "rule" (fixed or template text) or "llm" (a language model; LLM use is limited to CHK-NONTEXT, CHK-LINK, CHK-COLOR, CHK-SENSORY and CHK-TITLE). null when suggested_text is null.

method.description: Optional. "llm" when the written text came from a language model (an LLM-suggested title, alt text or link label); "rule" otherwise.

applied_text.description: Optional. The text written into the PDF by this repair.

enum: This report does not certify ADA Title II or WCAG 2.1 conformance.

session_id.description: Unique ID chosen by the tester (or staff), e.g. a UUID. Never reused.

setup.description: Pod-defined starting data. This pod needs none, so send {}.

CodeCoverage.description: Nonnegative integer counts with covered <= total. If measurement is unavailable, both counts are null (never 0) and basis explains why.
